extracted.intended_audience: aspiring creative writers / fiction writers seeking craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft principles and evaluative tests for writing fiction and other creative prose, distilled from Joyce Carol Oates's interviews and practice. Covers idea generation, language mastery, revision, subject/treatment, and ethical/psychological material concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Junction of Unique and Universal
rubrics_metrics.description: "I try to keep in mind the delicate relationship between what is unique, perhaps even eccentric, and what is universal. Only in this relationship is there a true subject, worthy of long hours of work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should balance the singular, specific or eccentric detail with themes or concerns that resonate more broadly; a strong subject arises when the particular and the universal intersect. Quality test: "Does the work bridge unique and universal?"

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment Matters More Than Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: "It isn't the subjects we write about but the seriousness and subtlety of our expression that determines the worth of our effort."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate writing by how thoughtfully and subtly the subject is handled rather than by whether the subject itself is conventionally 'interesting.' Quality test: "Does the writer treat the subject with seriousness and subtlety?"

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft + Inspiration (Private vision → Communal vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It's at the junction of private vision and the wish to create a communal, public vision that art and craft merge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art requires both inward, idiosyncratic vision and the craft to shape that vision into something communicable to readers; successful work negotiates private insight and public intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Personal as Material
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tap deeply into the personal." Use real events (own experience or news) as raw material; let them seep into the subconscious; emerge transformed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on personal/empathic material but transform it—do not simply report autobiographical facts. Let lived detail and news feed imagination so scenes and emotions feel lived-in and authentic without being mere reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea Germination / Let Ideas Incubate
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with an idea; let it "sink into unconsciousness." Imagine scenes, dialogue, characters intuitively; don't draft until the idea has had time to grow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for unconscious processing: imagine and rehearse scenarios mentally before committing to drafting. Avoid premature drafting; wait until the idea has depth and internal momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust the Unconscious
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust intuitive imagination and the unconscious to develop material and shape scenes/characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on intuition to surface surprising details and associations. Use conscious craft to later refine what the unconscious delivers, but give the unconscious permission to incubate the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of Language / Sentences Must Work
rubrics_metrics.description: "You have to have the language on the craft. You have to know how to divide it up and how the sentences work." / "Sentences must work — line-level mastery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line-level control is essential: syntax, rhythm, diction, and sentence construction must be deliberate and effective. Assess prose for sentence-level weight and precision: does the language carry the work?

rubrics_metrics.name: Read Deeply
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad, deep reading informs craft, expands possibilities, and supplies models and countermodels. Exposure to a wide range of styles and eras sharpens taste and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Daily / Discipline Over Inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Write daily — discipline matters more than inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular writing practice builds craft, output, and allows ideas to be refined; treat writing as a habit rather than waiting for sporadic inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with What Obsesses You
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with what obsesses you — write what you can't stop thinking about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects that generate sustained attention and compulsion; genuine obsession fuels depth, urgency, and sustained revision. Quality test: "Does the work emerge from genuine obsession, not just opportunity?"

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor the Unique Perspective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect and foreground the writer's particular viewpoint or vision rather than flattening voice into generic conventions; uniqueness is a resource when guided by craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Fear Darkness / Confront Difficult Material Carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't fear darkness — Oates is famous for confronting violence/death. Quality test: "Has the writer earned the dark/difficult material through care?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may engage with violent, dark, or disturbing subjects, but must earn their use through serious, careful treatment—avoid sensationalism or cheap shock; show ethical and artistic responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise Extensively ('Writing is Rewriting')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize revision as the core of craft: substantial rewriting is expected. Use revision to refine ideas, tighten language, and ensure that treatment, structure, and sentence-level work cohere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Engaged with the World (Gather Material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Live engaged with the world — the writer needs material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain curiosity and active engagement with society, news, and experience to supply raw material and insight. Being outwardly engaged fuels authenticity and relevance in fiction.
